description: The citation trail for this design-repo. Every token, section contract, template node sequence and motion config was measured from one of the sources below rather than inferred. These paths are relative to the PARENT project directory and deliberately do NOT appear in registry.manifest.json's entryPoints — a standalone copy of design-repo/ will not contain them, and extraction/verify_all.py downgrades citation checking to a warning in that case rather than failing.
gracefulDegradation: verify_all.py checks for a sibling `src/` directory. Present: every "path:line[-line]" citation is resolved against the real file and an out-of-range span fails the run. Absent: the check warns and is skipped. The repo therefore verifies clean both next to its source and on its own.

appSource.role: Authoritative for section ORDER, component composition and class strings. Where spec prose and the real component disagreed, the component won.

measurementSpecs.role: Authoritative for measured geometry, computed typography, colour tokens, asset inventory and decoded motion configs. Written from in-browser Playwright measurement of the live original (which is Next.js + Tailwind v4 + Framer Motion, so several values were read off its own compiled CSS and component source).

savedMirror.role: A saved copy of the original homepage plus per-route screenshots and raw measurement JSON (_reference/recon-b/*.json), used to settle disputes between spec prose and rendered reality.

informationArchitecture.role: Independently-built route/template/section map for the same project. Converged on the same 22 templates and 195 routes from the same route table, derived separately. Section ids differ by naming convention between the two documents; the route and template counts agree.
informationArchitecture.note: Added to the project AFTER this design-repo build began, so an earlier build note claiming no IA artifact existed is stale.

correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.claim: Section contracts declared motionIsClosed:true with an 11-field motionFieldSet.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.reality: 33 of 46 contracts carried motion keys outside their own declared set.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.resolution: The closure is correct for PageSpec emission; the CLAIM was imprecise. Added motionClosureScope and motionDocumentationFields to all 46 contracts, and updated compatibility/graph.json's MOTION_OBJECT_IS_CLOSED rule so the prose and the enforced code agree.

correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.reality: Enumerating templates.json showed 6 templates have no conversion.reassurance-cta: T-ARTICLE and T-PILLAR close with conversion.lead-magnet-cta instead.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.resolution: Exception list regenerated from the real node sequences. As drafted, the rule would have rejected 54 real, correct routes.

correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.claim: ONE_HERO_PER_PAGE exempted T-PRICING, implying a multi-hero page.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.reality: T-PRICING has ZERO hero.* nodes — its opener is pricing.single-plan.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.resolution: exceptionBasis records that the exemption is for a hero-LESS template.

correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.reality: T-ARTICLE legitimately chains two `listing` sections, and the validator could not read a prose exception.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.resolution: Added machine-readable exemptAdjacency / alwaysExemptCategories, which the validator actually reads, with the prose list kept in agreement.

correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.claim: A naive repeatability check compared (section, variant) counts against 1.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.reality: T-HOME, T-ESG and T-PARTNER each declare divider.leaf-band twice as two separate non-repeatable positional nodes.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.resolution: The check now compares against the template's OWN declared count. As written it rejected 4 real templates while still catching a true duplicate.

correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.claim: hero.home / hero.partner were each one HERO section.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.reality: Measured at 1440px from a fresh build, the opening wrapper is 3545px on / and 3788px on /partners/the-people-people-group — above the 3000px HERO limit; blocks 7-12 are a proof stack, not the page-opening composition.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.resolution: 2.0.0: split into hero.home / hero.partner (blocks 0-6) and the new proof.social-proof-stack (blocks 7-12). Re-measured: hero.home 1626px, hero.partner 1869px (warn), proof stack 1919px.

correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.claim: T-PILLAR's node list described the pillar page.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.reality: The real body interleaves 7 prose blocks with a stat row, 4 card groups, a vocabulary list, two headings, a FAQ and a reading list (src/data/pillar.js:144-323). The 1.0.0 list grouped each type once, and the node-order check compared against a de-duplicated list, so a faithful PageSpec was rejected.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.resolution: 2.0.0: T-PILLAR lists the real 18-unit order; the order check now walks the positional template list and allows in-place repetition only at repeatable positions.

correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.claim: Legal pages and article bodies were one content.rich-text node.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.reality: /privacy-policy's prose is 89% of its page (8326px of 9314px); /blog/35-creative-ideas-on-how-to-recognize-employees's body is 68%.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.resolution: 2.0.0: content.rich-text is repeatable on T-LEGAL / T-ARTICLE, one node per heading-bounded chapter / legal part (20 parts measured on /privacy-policy). The 35-ideas post has one heading only; its single chapter is whitelisted with an agent attestation.

correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.claim: Nav and footer carried no asset roles.
correctionsAppliedDuringBuild.reality: Nav.jsx renders the Evergreen logo; Footer.jsx renders the logo, social icons and a leaf.

knownEvidenceGaps: Long-form prose on the article, glossary, message-set, company-value, case-study and legal templates is deliberate placeholder copy sized to measured block heights. Titles, slugs, headings, labels and images are real. Copy budgets come from the measured line counts, not from the placeholder text.

Recon sampled 4 of 102 collection detail routes. Unsampled routes reuse their sibling's element counts, so a few document heights run 8-13% short of the original. Per-block geometry is exact; total page length drifts. Each template carries its own evidenceLevel.
Server-side form error strings were never observable (the originals post to server actions with no public endpoint) and are marked as stand-ins in the form contracts.
The original's third-party scheduler iframe is cross-origin; its interior could not be measured. The clone ships a static placeholder matched to the measured box.

The display serif is a substitution: the original uses a Typekit-bound face that cannot be self-hosted. The clone self-hosts Gloock at size-adjust 92.44%, chosen by measuring ~50 open serifs against the original's real text-advance widths. Section geometry is exact; cap-height runs ~2.7% short, and two headings sit under 2% wrap headroom.

Motion is SPECIFIED, NOT YET ANIMATED in the app. Every leaf renders in its correct pre-animation position with the right class name and the scroll-track hook is exposed, but nothing animates yet. The configs here are decoded from the original, not observed running in the clone.

Section heights (sectionHeights) were measured at 1440px only, on ONE representative route per template (the tallest route rendering the full node set); other routes of multi-route templates were not measured.
Visual parity against the live evergreen.so was NOT measured in the 2.0.0 revision (no live capture); only the built clone was measured.

Generation-mode leakage detection is string-based (normalised substrings and hashed 5-word shingles); paraphrased or translated source copy is not detected, and the derived pattern lists have not been reviewed by a human.

sectionHeights.measuredWith: extraction/measure_sections.mjs (headless Chromium via Playwright) against `vite preview` of a fresh `vite build` of the clone; DOM mapping from extraction/section-dom-map.json
sectionHeights.scope: one representative route per template (the tallest served route that renders the full node set); heights in CSS px at a 1440px-wide viewport

nodes.chapterHeading: Transfers outside the EU or EEA
